questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: How to keep food fresh in the fridge
Food waste and people trying to reduce it
Why supermarkets import fruit
How to grow avocados
questions.why: Neil says they'll talk about food waste and meet people trying to stop us throwing good food away.

questions.q: According to the UN, how much of the food we grow is thrown away?
options: About a tenth
About half
Around two thirds
One third
questions.why: Sam says one third of the food we grow ends up in the rubbish bin.

questions.q: What problem with imported summer fruit in winter is mentioned?
options: It adds to carbon emissions and waste
It tastes much worse than local fruit
It is too expensive for most people
It is often unsafe to eat raw
questions.why: Sam says flying in summer fruit increases carbon emissions as well as waste.

questions.q: What was farmer Josefina Arcay's problem with the middlemen?
options: They never paid her on time for her fruit
They only bought avocados, nothing else
She had no control and got lower prices
They sold her food abroad without asking
questions.why: She says they'd say it's too expensive and offer half the price, so she had no control.

questions.q: What did Josefina set up to solve this?
options: A new supermarket in her home town
An online shop linking buyers and farmers
A company of middlemen to sell her food
A restaurant using only local food
questions.why: She started an online shop to connect shoppers with farmers directly, without supermarkets.

questions.q: How much food waste happens after people have bought the food, according to the UN?
options: 10 percent
33 percent
60 percent
90 percent
questions.why: The UN estimates 60 percent of food waste happens this way.

questions.q: Why does Solveiga Pakstaite say use-by dates are often too early?
options: Supermarkets want people to buy more food
They are printed too early by mistake
Farmers ask for shorter dates on labels
They plan for food being stored badly
questions.why: She says they calculate for the worst-case scenario, since they don't know which product will be stored wrongly.

questions.q: What is the result of these cautious use-by dates?
options: A lot of safe food gets thrown away
More people get food poisoning
Food becomes more expensive
Supermarkets sell less food
questions.why: Sam says it protects customers, but a lot of safe-to-eat food gets thrown away.
